records.notes: We raise grassfed beef, pasture raised chicken, and heritage breed pasture raised pork here in Texas. Our animals have room to roam - rooting, grazing, and pecking at the grasses, bugs, and whatever else they find in the sunshine. They are not given hormones or antibiotics. Our feed blend for our chickens and hogs is corn and soy free. We rotate our animals throughout the pastures, allowing ample time between rotations for the soil and grasses to regenerate.

records.notes: Amber Oaks Ranch is a 70-acre homestead just south of Thorndale, TX (about 35 miles ENE of Austin). It was established in December 2015 by John & Molly Pantalone. The purposes of Amber Oaks Ranch are threefold: to provide a secure future for ourselves and family, to put into practice the regenerative agricultural practices we’ve learned, and to provide a wholesome experience to our friends and neighbors. The cornerstone of Amber Oaks Ranch is a pastured meat-based operation. We raise beef, pork, and poultry on pasture – the way it should be. In the future, we hope to build a customer butchering facility and teaching homesteading classes to our friends and neighbors. We believe that it is vitally important to feed the mind, body, and spirit with unadulterated truth. We are alarmed by the current state of education and agriculture and are concerned for the welfare of the people we love. To this end, we have established Amber Oaks Ranch in order to help people reclaim their freedom through independent living and to establish wellbeing through healthy nutrition.

Discovered through Callahan County seat search (https://www.localharvest.org/baird-tx/farms). Listing last updated Jan 21, 2025. American Criollo Beef Alliance presents 100% grass-fed, pasture raised Criollo beef. Criollo beef is exceptionally tender and very lean. Criollo has been proven in DNA testing to rival Kobe beef (from Wagyu cattle) for tenderness and Angus beef for quality. ACBA has each animal DNA tested for tenderness and meat quality (marbling) before entering the Certified Criollo Beef Program and sold to the consumer, thus ensuring consistent quality. Criollo cattle were brought to the "New World" from the high desert plains of Andalusia in Southern Spain on Columbus's second voyage. Superbly adapted for survival in the hostile environments of the North American southwest, these hardy cattle thrive on available forage. They are renowned for their hardiness, fertility, gentle nature and longevity. They are easy on the land, tending to improve a pasture, rather than destroy it. Criollo cattle naturally self-rotate through a pasture, utilizing every square foot of acreage, rather than concentrating on any one area. records.notes: Beauty’s Community Garden is located in Independence Heights–the first African American municipality in Texas and one of 40 food deserts in Houston. Purchased property in 1926 by her grandparents, Ernest and Beauty Leno, Yvette Leno later inherited the land. In 1991, a devastating fire destroyed the family’s homestead. In 2012, Yvette repurposed the land into a community garden she named after her grandmother, “Beauty.” Today, Beauty’s Community Garden is growing into the vision Yvette imagined, a place for community members to come together to access and learn about healthy whole foods they can plant. The garden is a natural place to plant roots and connect the benefits of choosing healthy foods by learning about nutrition and its impact on a person’s physical and mental well-being. Beauty's Community Garden runs over 6,000 square feet with a 20 ft container. The garden features community-connected spaces where 10-15 volunteers support the garden weekly, and a variety of fresh produce and herbs are grown and sustained. We provide community service hours and hands-on gardening clinics with our community partners, businesses, schools, and community groups within the garden and throughout the larger Houston community.

records.notes: At Behind the Oaks Farm, we raise grass-fed beef, pasture-raised pork, poultry, eggs, and other farm products using regenerative farming practices that help restore the land while producing nourishing food for our community. Located in Schertz, Texas, our family farm focuses on improving soil health, supporting local food systems, and raising animals with compassion and care. Through rotational grazing and a closed-loop composting system, we work to build healthy soils, reduce waste, and leave the land better than we found it. You can shop with us online, visit our farm store, or find us at farmers markets throughout the San Antonio area.

Discovered through Harris County seat search (https://www.localharvest.org/houston-tx/farms). Listing last updated Jan 21, 2025. Local honey from Houston inside the 610 Loop bees! Our Italian bees reside year round inside the Loop and forage to a four-mile radius including Bellaire, West University, Southside Place and certain other inside the Loop neighborhoods of Houston producing sweet, flavorful, and 100% natural honey. Our honey is unprocessed and contains no additives of any kind. We use no chemical treatments in providing care to our honey bees. Our honey is straight from the hive to our jars! We harvest honey from our bees generally between May - October depending on weather and nectar flows in our surrounding area. Our honey "Miele Millefiori" translated as "Thousand Flowers Honey" is a tribute to the Italian origin of our honey bees and is available year round while supplies last.

records.notes: Bernhardt's Fruit & Veggie Farm is a family-owned operation on thirteen acres in Elgin. Our mission is to provide chemical and pesticide-free, locally grown, fresh produce to the people of Central Texas. We have a young 70-tree orchard consisting of pecan and various fruit trees and grow a wide variety of berries, grapes, and vegetables year-round. After graduating in 2011, they decided to farm full time and built a licensed commercial kitchen on the farm so that they could make value-added goods out of the things they grow like sorbet, pickles, jam, salsa, sauces, pesto and prepared entrees. The Bernhardts moved to the family homestead in 2007 to look after Alex’s 88-year old dad and started gardening for fun. While working on his business degree at Concordia, the hobby continued to grow and grow and grow.

records.notes: At Bijou’s Blooms, we are a small, first-generation farm rooted in Liberty Hill, Texas, dedicated to growing seasonal vegetables, herbs, and cut flowers that thrive in the Central Texas climate. We specialize in heat-loving, locally adapted plants, fresh bouquets, and garden-ready seedlings, all grown with care, intention, and a deep respect for the land. Our farm stand operates on a simple, trust-based system, offering an ever-changing selection of locally grown goods alongside thoughtfully curated, garden-inspired products from nearby makers. Beyond the stand, we also provide garden consultations, installations, and hands-on classes designed to help our community grow their own food and reconnect with the rhythm of the seasons. At Bijou’s Blooms, everything we offer is rooted in supporting local — from the soil our plants are grown in to the flowers in each bouquet and the small businesses we proudly feature alongside our own.

Our animals are field harvested from over 150 different ranches located in central and south Texas. The deer and antelope we harvest are free-ranging, feeding on natural grasses and other vegetation. Since the animals are wild and roaming on large areas, we use a unique field harvesting system designed by us and approved by the Texas Department of Health. records.notes: Dear Friends and Neighbors, My name is Donna Beavers, and together with Tomas Holguin, I am pleased to introduce you to Bulah’s Best Farm. We have called Bulah, Texas home for more than 25 years and have been dedicated beekeepers for the past 18 years. I am a retired medical microbiologist, and Tomas is a retired teacher. Our backgrounds in science and education naturally led us to a deep appreciation for the intricate world of honeybees and the vital role they play in our ecosystem and overall well-being. Over the years, our farm has included milk goats, a Jersey cow, heritage pigs, poultry, and sheep. While those chapters were rewarding, our focus today is centered on caring for our bees and producing high-quality, raw honey. We use environmentally responsible practices that support the health of our bees, the land, and the broader community. Our passion for learning has taken us abroad to study alternative beekeeping practices and apitherapy in Romania, Mexico, Turkey, and Colombia. These experiences have enriched our approach and strengthened our commitment to producing honey and apitherapy products that are pure, wholesome, and handled with care. At Bulah’s Best Farm, we offer a variety of raw honey and bee byproducts harvested to preserve their natural flavor and beneficial properties. records.notes: About Our Beef Our mission is to provide your family with great tasting, ethically raised, sustainable, Texas beef direct from our farm to your family table. Read more about our operations below! Grass Fed, Grain Finished Marbling is one of the most important influences on the taste of great beef and gives steaks, like the ribeye, that rich, buttery flavor. Our beef is grain finished for a minimum of 120 days, which creates these fantastic flavors and premium steaks that grade as USDA high choice or prime. We guarantee this is some of the best tasting beef you will ever have! Ethically Raised We believe in treating our animals humanely and raising them in a stress free, comfortable environment. Traditionally, cattle are shipped to feedlots where they are confined in small feedlot pens with hundreds of animals for 90-120 days of grain finishing. Our animals are pasture raised 100% of the time, encouraging the cows’ natural behaviors and minimizing undue stress to the animals. We provide over 300 acres of open pasture for roaming and grazing, as well as 24/7 access to clean water, shade, hay, feed, and minerals. Unlike traditional feedlots, we do not restrict our cows from grass and natural forage during the finishing process. Our custom grain finishing program utilizes free choice self-feeding with the animal remaining on pasture. Dale Family Farms is a small farm owned and managed by two generations of Dales. Located in South Central Kansas, we are striving to be sustainable. To do this, we have learned that we must better utilize our resources through improved grazing practices and reduced reliance on fuel and equipment. Over the last few years, we have realized that letting our animals remain in their natural environment doing what they do best, grazing, will be our key to sustainability. Our beef comes from cattle that are finished on a strict forage diet of legumes, grasses, and forbs. The beef we sell contains no synthetic growth hormones and no antibiotics. When prepared properly, we have found that grass-finished beef is as tender as grain fed beef with a much richer, fuller, beef flavor. Beef is available by the cut, wholes, halves and quarters. Laying hens are allowed to free range during the day, foraging for green grass, seeds and insects. This "salad bar" approach to their diet improves the flavor and texture of the eggs they produce. We rotate pasture grazing on native Texas grasses. We have two natural ponds for water use. We feel our cows are the most content cows in east Texas! Our start in organic grass-fed beef came from necessity due to illness, and we want to help others to eat healthily. We understand firsthand the importance of chemical-free, natural fresh foods. Our beef is dry aged for 21 days to provide tender tasty beef, and wrapped in cellophane to help avoid contamination of beef with dioxins and phthalates from plastic wrapping. People with severe allergies or history of cancer can appreciate the benefit of our cellophane use. Our butcher in Kaufman, TX will cut meat to your specifications and use vacuum wrap if cellophane is not desired. We will take reservations for half sides and half split sides of beef for 2025 . records.notes: Feathered Fork Farms is a 30-acre homestead located about 30 miles Southeast of Waco in the rural town of Lott, Texas. Established in February of 2022, Bo and Candice Johnson decided to take their agricultural heritage and passion to create fresh produce and meat products on their farm. Candice Johnson has been farming and ranching her whole life, but Feathered Fork is where she began her own venture. “Feathered Fork” started out with just chickens which is where the “feathered” part of the name came from. Green Wolf Vertical Farm employs a closed-loop hydroponic vertical tower system. Intensive greenhouse management is used to greatly reduce environmental waste as opposed to conventional soil farming. Water and nutrient use is greatly minimized in our re-circulating drip system. Approximately 10 gallons of water a day is used in this type of system. Our vertical towers are an intense growing system that can produce in 100 square feet what traditional farming produces in 400 square feet. We are not Certified Organic, however we do use similar growing practices. Grow from organic, non-GMO seed Beneficial insects for pest control Balanced hydroponic nutrients By using these methods our greenhouse has very little if any impact on the surrounding environment and keeps our farm operating as environmentally friendly as possible.

We are a small family farm on the Texas/New Mexico state line, raising grass fed - finished Devon/Red Angus cross since 2009. They graze on native pasture in the summer and use winter annuals with free choice hay plus access to stockpiled grass the rest of the year. Our focus is to build soil health; therefore, we use no chemicals on our pastures. Our cattle are raised from birth to market in a gentle, stress free way, with no grain, antibiotics, or added growth hormones. We use rotational grazing to give the cattle the best choice of grass, practicing this since 1996.The beef is 22-26 months old when ready to be processed, which is done in our local USDA Texas facility. They are available in halves or as a whole beef. By USDA standards, our beef has been rated as Choice. Call for the availability of our grass finished flavorful tender beef.

records.notes: Located in Elgin TX, Hot Spell Farm is a worker operated farm that is people and Earth first. We are making a collective commitment to sustain joy and community through shared land and vegetables. Currently, few cooperative opportunities for produce growers exist in our home state of Texas; there are limited, if not nonexistent models for the farm we want to build our community. The typical farm operation might be spearheaded by individuals, spouses, and well-endowed benefactors… We’re none of those. Hot Spell is the brainchild of four farmworkers who previously worked together on farms not-our-own. Our intentions and dreams as an equitable, multi-owner farm were created from a shared desire to carve space for non-traditional paths to farming in Central Texas. Our vision is to increase access to nutritionally dense and southern-adapted produce for the metro Austin area and beyond. In hopes of breaking patterns of profit-driven burnout, our work-centered operation is a hopeful step in creating a participatory model for first-gen workers: you don’t have to do it alone. We sell our produce at the farmers market, offer a 12-week CSA with local pickup options, and sell directly to wholesale buyers. Visit our website to learn more and connect. HAVE FUN, BE HOT, GROW GOOD FOOD.

A decade of diligence to that task allowed nature to do her work, and the farm reached the stage where the measured introduction of complementary livestock will complete the farm's restoration and transform it into a self-sustaining agricultural enterprise. Jolie Vue grows heritage cattle and pastured pigs and brings those meats, with free range chickens and eggs to your door, once a month, in an ice chest which we provide. They also have access to floorless hoop houses moved to fresh grass daily, for shelter during the day and security at night. records.notes: We are a community farm & garden located in the historic town of Joppa, just six miles south of downtown Dallas. Joppa was founded in 1872 by Henry Hines; an emancipated slave. It is one of the last Freedman towns in Texas. Although its history is rich, Joppa has endured extreme marginalization. Though nestled between the lush wetlands of the Trinity River and the Great Trinity Forest, Joppa was federally declared a food desert. Joppy Momma’s Farm vows to change that by providing healthy, affordable foods for the community. We aim to empower, educate and create greater opportunities for health, wellness and self-sufficiency through sustainable, regenerative agriculture. We are committed to restoring, rebuilding and regenerating the community one seed at a time! We provide produce to our community and sell at local farmers markets and local pop-ups. We are working to build an on-site market to better serve the community with fresh produce and other healthy eating options. Come down to Joppy Momma’s Farm the third Saturday of every month to help volunteer!

Discovered through Hansford County seat search (https://www.localharvest.org/spearman-tx/farms). Listing last updated Jan 21, 2025. Welcome to Jornada Alpacas. We were looking for livestock that would fit on our acreage (5 acres), be relatively easy to work with AND be enjoyable to be around. What a perfect fit with alpaca! Our goal is to breed and raise quality alpaca for the future of the national herd and quality fiber for the production of luxurious yarns and a wide range of clothing made from their amazing fiber. Last but not least, for the "shear" enjoyment of it. I have had the pleasure of to learn spinning, weaving and now knitting the fiber. Working with Alpaca is a truely "hands on" experience. Alpaca fleece is the natural fiber harvested from an alpaca. It is light weight or heavy weight, depending on how it is spun. It is soft, durable, luxurious and silky natural fiber.

records.products: Back in a time when agriculture was deeply ingrained in our society, the concept of Farm to Table wasn’t just a buzzword; it was the standard. Fast forward to today, and the accessibility of ranch-raised beef has become a premium and elusive commodity for many. At JT2 Beef, we set out to change that narrative. Our family-owned and operated ranch, rooted in the heart of East Texas, was founded on the principles of bringing back the traditional Farm-to-Table way of enjoying quality, all-natural meat. We believe that everyone should have affordable access to high-quality pasture-raised beef, just like in the old days.

JX Ranch Natural Beef - So good... and so good for you! is grass-fed, grass-finished and dry-aged for 14-21 days for optimum tenderness and flavor. Our cattle are born and raised on our 7,000 acre ranch and graze our native pastures living the way nature intended. We guarantee that our cattle have never received any antibiotics, growth-hormones, animal bi-products, ionophores, insecticides or any chemicals of any kind. Our pastures are never fertilized nor sprayed with any pesticides. We harvest our beef at a younger age which results in tender and flavorful meat. Tom and I practice holistic range management and regenerative grazing methods, and handle the cattle quietly and gently to avoid any stress. (Tom is a popular speaker at events throughout the State and recipient of many grazing awards.) In the spring and in the fall we offer whole, half and quarter Custom Cut beef. You can chose from several New Mexico butchers and we'll take your cow to them where you then pick up your meat. Visit our website LEANNATURALBEEF.COM to see what our customers have to say about our delicious tender beef or call us at 575-403-6904 to order or for questions.

records.notes: Discovered through Crockett County seat search (https://www.localharvest.org/ozona-tx/farms). Listing last updated Jan 21, 2025. La Cabra Meat is a family owned business that produces pastured goat, lamb and poultry. We are located ten miles north of Junction on Highway 83. The Holistic Goal at La Cabra Meat is to ensure nutrient dense, clean meats that are raised on our native pasture. La Cabra Meat uses Holistic Management production systems that are measured by the triple bottom line of profit, increased soil fertility and quality of life. The goats are Spanish-Boer crosses. There is a spring and fall kid crop. They free range on the wonderful browse and pasture the ranch has to offer. When they have reached 40-50 pounds, usually around 6 months of age they are processed. The broiler operation is made up of Freedom Rangers and Heritage White meat birds. They are raised in a brooder until old enough to enjoy their life rotating on fresh pasture in their chicken tractor that is moved every day. The broilers are supplemented with Non-GMO and Non-soy Hugelland feed milled in Fredericksburg, Texas. The lambs come from a show line of rambouillet bucks and ewes. They are born in the early spring and are ready for processing by mid to late June. Like the goats they free range on native pastureland.

We are seeing a large annual increase in the number of people who really care about the quality of the food they consume. These increasing numbers of consumers are using their purchasing power to positively change agricultural practices, because we all want better food. Utilizing impressive technological advances in animal husbandry, fencing technology, geospatial mapping, renewable energy, moisture capture, irrigation tapes, and disease recognition of the last 80 years along with regenerative practices utilized prior to the industrial revolution, we are poised to regenerate our soil and water while sequestering carbon. We not only utilize these important concepts on our farm, we teach them here, and we invite our customers to visit and see for themselves. records.notes: Mushroom Street Farms began as a small experiment with big potential. During the latter days of the COVID-19 pandemic, Warren Gwartney started growing mushrooms in a tiny tent in his guest room. As a longtime web and app developer, he spent his days staring at screens, and cultivating mushrooms became an unexpected yet rewarding escape. What started as a hobby quickly turned into a passion for science, agriculture, and food. Fascinated by the incredible world of fungi, Warren immersed himself in learning everything he could about gourmet mushrooms. Before long, he was growing more than he could possibly eat, so he shared them with friends and neighbors—who immediately wanted more. Demand kept growing, and soon, Mushroom Street Farms was born. Now, with a dedicated team and a new retail space in Deep Ellum, Mushroom Street Farms is more than just a farm—it’s a hub for mushroom education, culinary inspiration, and community connection. From supplying top chefs and restaurants to hosting events and tastings, Mushroom Street Farms is on a mission to share the magic of mushrooms with the world. Visit our website to order!

Our milk comes from a happy, healthy herd of Guernsey and Jersey cows that graze freely on lush pastures, ensuring they produce the best milk possible. What sets our raw milk apart is that it is local, grass fed and A2A2, meaning it comes from cows that produce a specific type of beta-casein protein that many people find easier to digest. This makes it a fantastic option for families looking to enjoy the benefits of raw milk without the discomfort that some experience with conventional dairy products. By participating in our herdshare program, you not only gain access to this incredible milk but also actively support local farming practices that prioritize animal welfare and environmental sustainability. records.notes: Our Family Farms TX is a family owned and operated dairy farm in Los Fresnos, TX. We produce raw cow's milk, specifically A2A2 milk that can be enjoyed by everyone - even if you're lactose intolerant! Our milk is triple-filtered and rigorously tested before milking to ensure that no pathogens are introduced. This means that you receive only the healthiest and purest milk, straight from our happy cows to your table. We sell our milk using a herdshare agreement, which is required to purchase raw milk and/or dairy products. Once you have bought into the herd, you can legally obtain raw milk and dairy products from your farmer. Every time you want to collect your allotment (1/2 gallon, 1 gallon, etc) you will reimburse the farmer for boarding, feeding, and milking, bottling, and caring for your part of the herd. Learn more by visiting our website and contact us with any questions you have!

They graze on local grass or local hay. We do give them a snack at milking time of Equine Total which is a natural product developed by a Texas Veterinarian. We take great care in making sure that our cows are happy and relaxed producing thick creamy sweet milk. My family drinks this milk everyday and we make the most glorious butter, cheese, yogurt and fabulous ice cream. We are not a Grade A Raw dairy so we can only offer this milk for animal use. Since we do baby our cows they have been producing much more than when we first got them and I just hate to throw this wonderful raw milk on the ground. So if you would like to try out a gallon of our milk to see if it suits your purposes, the first gallon is on us. You are also welcome to come out and watch us milk or try hand milking yourself. Bring the kids we have lots of animals to see and pet.

records.notes: Pure Pastures is a family owned, multi-species grazing operation, run in partnership by the Eubank and Moorman families. Our families' passions inspired our interest in regenerative and sustainable agriculture, and our drive to implement it’s practices on our ranch. Since 2019, Pure Pastures has been holistically managing our animals in a way that revitalizes the ranch’s natural resources; working WITH nature, instead of against her. The Eubanks have been ranching since 2015, using trial and error to perfect their rotational grazing practices; striving to provide the most flavorful and nutrient dense meat to their community, while rebuilding topsoil and the native prairie landscape that once dominated the Hill Country. With our rotational grazing practices, we are able to raise top quality grass fed & finished beef and lamb, and pasture raised, heritage breed pork. Our cattle, pigs, and sheep live their entire lives the way they are supposed to live: out on the land. We are proud to be stewards of the Texas Hill Country, and proud to be on your family's table!

records.notes: Raised Wild Texas is a private closed-herd ranch located in Italy, Texas. Through regenerative ranching practices, our cattle are 100% grass fed and grass finished, eating a variety of native grass species and forage that is found directly on our ranch. Our beef is free of all vaccines, hormones, and antibiotics, providing the cleanest, nutrient dense beef for our customers. We have developed a close relationship with a USDA processing facility in Malone, Texas where we process our cattle. From individual cuts to quarters, halves and wholes, Raised Wild Texas can meet you and your friends and family’s needs when it comes to high-quality beef.

Discovered through Baylor County seat search (https://www.localharvest.org/seymour-tx/farms). Listing last updated Jan 21, 2025. Because of the drought we've had to put off our Dairy Dreams. But....we are looking to start an outdoor preschool!! Look up the Waldkindergarten or Forest Kindergarten to get an idea of what it will look like.:o) As a previous homeschooling family we understand how important hands-on educational opportunities are, and we want to offer a place where children can begin to understand what makes a working farm tick. Why do some farms have milk all year, while others don't? Why are there more eggs in the spring? Why does the grocery store have tomatoes in December but the Farmer's Market doesn't? These questions and more can be asked and answered right here. I delight in sharing the changes, beyond wearing a coat or wearing a swimsuit, that the seasons bring.......allowing people to become more connected to the world they live in and the food they eat.

records.notes: Restoration Fields Farm is a micro farm and community market based at the historic 1919 Young School in Ranger, Texas (Recorded Texas Historic Landmark, 2024). We grow seasonal vegetables and cut flowers using no-till, soil-building practices and focus on keeping food and farm goods truly local—grown, made, and shared right here in our region. From May through October, we host a weekly Thursday farmers market that brings together 5–20 local vendors, making it easy for families to shop directly from the people who raise and craft what they sell. Whether it’s our own produce and blooms or goods from our vendor community, we prioritize short supply chains, transparent sourcing, and relationships you can actually meet in person.

records.notes: At Rusty Star Ranch, our mission is to sustainably produce high-quality goat cheeses, raw goat milk, pastured pork, and grass-fed beef, which we sell directly to our local and regional communities. This is not a side business or hobby—it is our full-time livelihood. We are proud to be one of the few licensed goat dairies in Texas, making us a vital resource for families who have dairy sensitivities and rely on alternative options like raw goat milk and goat cheese. We also raise Dexter Cattle and live on pasture and are never given grain, along with raising pastured raised pork. Our commitment to sustainable practices, animal welfare, and community-based agriculture positions us as a trusted source for ethically raised, nutritionally valuable dairy and meats. *PREORDER NECESSARY TO PURCHASE RAW MILK* You can also purchase our products from our partners (Bali Family Farm, One Milk Agent, Acht Kinder Farmers Co-Op).

Listing last updated Jan 21, 2025. 100% Grass-fed and grass-finished beef, pastured pork, pastured chicken, pastured eggs, pastured turkey. We are a small family farming operation dedicated to raising our animals right. This means no genetically modified feeds, no chemicals, no hormone ear tags, no confinement, no unnecessary medications (only used in emergencies!), no mistreatment, and no inappropriate feeds. We use absolutely no soy and no non-organic corn. In return for raising our animals this way, they produce for us the most flavorful, tender meat products that are packed full of nutrients. Our eggs are rich golden orange simply because our birds are out foraging on bugs all day long--we don't have to cheat and feed them marigolds! We practice intensive pasture management, including rotating cows, chickens, and pigs across our pastures. We offer farm tours and farm days from time to time in hopes of reconnecting families with their food sources. We want you to come and see how your food is raised so you KNOW it's healthy for your family!

records.notes: Early in 2020, the Women’s Empowerment Group of FAM Houston began dreaming about a place to grow fresh produce. Thanks to the support of local partners, a new community farm—Shamba Ya Amani—was established and continues to grow week by week. The farm is run by resettled refugees, immigrants, and local Houstonians with the hope that this agricultural endeavor will serve as a model for increasing food access and human connection. Our farmers tend their own dedicated raised beds, and these same farmers also make collective decisions about our ½-acre community field—what to grow and how to harvest and distribute the crops. Women representing around 30+ households have made commitments to growing food at the farm. Shamba Ya Amani has flourished so that FAM Houston has hired a team of part-time farm stewards who plant, weed, water, harvest, and prepare crops for market. They determine weekly tasks, encourage others to participate, and collaboratively plan the next growing season. Our regular community volunteer days are Saturdays from 9 am–noon. You’re welcome to join us! Service hours can be earned for various individuals and groups.

records.notes: In Spring 2017, to the dismay of our friends and family, we abruptly sold our house in central Austin and traded city living for life on Shirttail Creek Farm just outside Brenham, TX (about halfway between Austin and Houston). It would be fair to call this a leap of faith... After a 15 year career in Digital Advertising and chasing the life we thought we wanted we realized we were on a path that wasn’t actually fulfilling for us. So with two kids in tow (1 and 3 at the time) we set out to lay down some roots on a farm where we could raise our kids, and build a life full of meaning and purpose. Were we naive to the realities of what we were doing? Absolutely. But if it wasn't for ignorance and a desire for adventure, nobody would ever take any risk at all! And so the journey began. Moving to the farm was the beginning of an awakening for us. Yes we moved away from our favorite coffee shops, our friends, and our comfort zones, but we also thrust ourselves into a life that didn't allow us to hide when the weather turned bad or call for help every time the tractor broke down or an animal got sick. It was also the beginning of our evolution around how we view food. Before moving to the farm, we shopped at the big fancy 'granola' grocery stores in Austin and bought foods with packaging that had all the right buzz words. records.notes: Sovereignty Ranch is a regenerative farm and community destination located on over 200 acres in the Texas Hill Country near Bandera. The ranch produces a wide variety of farm-fresh foods, including seasonal vegetables, fruits, herbs, pasture-raised meats, eggs, raw milk and other dairy, sourdough breads, and other locally made goods. Products are available through online ordering, farm pick-ups, and local delivery, making it easy for customers to access fresh, thoughtfully grown food. In addition to its farm offerings, Sovereignty Ranch features a farm-to-table restaurant highlighting ingredients grown and raised on-site, as well as event spaces and accommodations including cottages, farmhouses, and glamping stays. The ranch also hosts workshops, retreats, and community gatherings centered on regenerative agriculture, food, and connection to the land. Whether you’re looking for fresh local produce, artisan foods, a memorable dining experience, or a Hill Country getaway, Sovereignty Ranch offers a unique way to engage with Texas-grown food and farming!

Discovered through Andrews County seat search (https://www.localharvest.org/andrews-tx/farms). Listing last updated Jan 21, 2025. Started in 1973, by my grandparents, we sold pecans a few years in a row when the trees started producing. The drip irrigation system began to fail & some trees died off, but many were spared. We aren't a huge operation, just family - my parents, my 2 children, & other family members pitching in from time to time, no employees. Located just outside the city limits, we are lucky to have wildlife such as fox, hawks, dove, quail, bobcat, coyote, & of course various snake, lizard & other crawly species. Oh, and I can't forget to mention the excellent number of Texas horned lizards (horny toads) that enjoy life at our place! We've had a couple of really good pecan crops the last few years, & have decided to sell some. Our trees are never treated with pesticides or herbicides, just west Texas well water & rain when we're blessed with it.

records.source_name: Texas Center for Local Food — Farms & Ranches
records.notes: We are a family business with a clear mission: to provide the highest quality agricultural products and services, God’s intended way. That means respecting creation, stewarding the land responsibly, caring for animals properly, and producing nutrient-dense food with transparency and honesty. Our operation integrates cattle, goats, laying hens, broiler chickens, and vermiculture, each playing a specific role in land restoration. Our cattle are managed through adaptive, multi-paddock, intensive grazing. By moving them frequently and allowing adequate recovery, we stimulate grass growth, improve water infiltration, and build organic matter in the soil. Goats help us manage brush and invasive species—especially mesquite—without chemicals. They allow us to restore balance where mechanical or chemical methods would further damage the land. Our pasture-raised laying hens and broiler chickens follow grazing animals, spreading nutrients, reducing pests, and adding another layer of biological activity to the soil while producing high-quality food. Our vermiculture operation produces biologically rich compost "tea" helping us rebuild soil life and fertility from the ground up. Healthy soils are living systems, and worms are a key part of restoring that life. Everything we do is intentional. Each enterprise supports the land, the animals, and the people who depend on them. Visit our website to place an order!

records.notes: Nestled in the scenic Texas Hill Country at Trails End Ranch, our devoted rancher, Ashly Martin, raises 100% Iberico pigs with the utmost care and respect. These lucky pigs spend their days happily foraging on native plants, including Texas Live Oak acorns, mesquite beans (their favorite!), prickly pear cacti, and more. Plus, they enjoy premium feed and TLC for over 18 months—three times longer than commercial pigs. We're committed to delivering not just USDA fresh cuts, but also the finest American artisan charcuterie, straight from our ranch to your deli counter. With an active lifestyle and exceptional genetic characteristics, Iberico pigs produce some of the healthiest meat available anywhere. Texas Iberico pasture-raised pigs are never given antibiotics. Texas Iberico is dedicated to practicing pasture rotation, a cornerstone of the Spanish "Dehesa" approach, to aid in land restoration. In a single grazing season, the pigs eliminate numerous invasive plant species resulting from excessive cattle ranching, paving the way for the revival of native grasses.

We've been growing our certified organic shiitake mushrooms year round since 1990. We're a sustainable, woman-owned, family farm. We don't use the Chinese shiitake logs which so many so-called "local farms" use. We prepare our own logs, beginning with hardwood sawdust from a Texas lumber mill. All of our inputs are from the USA. Our clamshell packages are made in America from 100% recycled and recyclable PETE which is basically, water bottles. We also pack 5 pound bulk cases in cardboard boxes made in Texas. Look for our shiitakes in Whole Foods and other stores that promote local organic food and on the menu in restaurants that feature local food. Thank-you for supporting local farmers!

Nestled in the Piney Woods of East Texas sits The Farm at Bald Hill, a family farm focusing on regenerative agriculture and sustainability with a goal of changing the way people eat. Regenerative agriculture is the practice of conserving and rehabilitating the land in order to strengthen the health and vitality of the soil. We do this through high efficiency rotational grazing and effective water management, thus ensuring the highest quality of life for our animals. We are diligent in the processes employed to maintain our high standards. All of the calves are fed and finished for 16-18 months on a variety of natural, protein and nutrient rich grasses. Our pigs are on pasture for 8 months, rooting and fertilizing the soil to aid in keeping it healthy. Our chickens are rotated daily onto fresh pasture. No grain. No corn. No chemicals. No hormones. No antibiotics. Ever. The animals live in a harmonious balance with nature resulting in top quality protein that's good for you and for the environment.

Triple J Organics, LLC. was established in 1995 by Jesse Lozano of Mission, Texas. It first began as a one-man hobby having planted and grafted almost every tree on an abondoned 10 acre orchard his father, Jesus Lozano, and his father-in-law, Jose Macias helped him to purchase after the 1983 freeze. As the trees produced more fruit, the family was the main source of labor. The first packing began in the backyard of our home in Pharr, Tx. Fruit was picked and loaded on the back of the pickup truck and was packed by the family in the backyard. As the business began to grow, Jesse built a packing shed on 14702 N Trosper Rd. Each year Jesse had to expand the square ft area of the packing shed to keep up with the demands of the market. Triple J Organics, LLC is known for and takes pride in its fresh and tree-ripened organic fruit. Jesse oversees the grove care involved in the production of organic fruit, as well as the picking and packing of every box to ensure its wholesome goodness.

records.notes: VRDNT Farm is a bio-intensive farm growing flavorful and colorful vegetables for Central Texans. Owner/Operator Becky Hume spent over 10 years working on Organic and sustainable farms before taking the leap to start her own in 2019. VRDNT’s mission is simple: to nourish the land and local community by growing high quality, nutrient dense, super fresh veggies. VRDNT uses no synthethetic chemical inputs or GMO seeds. Instead, beneficial insects and a balanced ecosystem are encouraged to provide nourishment to the soil, which then supports strong and resilient plants. All of this adds up to you receiving the highest quality, clean, and nutrient dense vegetables- visit the website to learn more!

records.notes: Discovered through Dallam County seat search (https://www.localharvest.org/dalhart-tx/farms). Listing last updated Jan 21, 2025. The W Diamond L ranch was founded in 1919 by A.F. Willett and his wife Bessie. Grandma and Grandpa Willett left Oklahoma and moved to northeastern New Mexico to homestead. They also created the W Diamond L brand for horses and cattle in New Mexico at this time. Today the northern half of the original ranch is run by Suzanne Bennefield, a granddaughter of the Willetts, and her husband Ted. Their son Jeremy also lives on the ranch and helps out. The ranch raises commercial cattle, quarter horses, paint horses, and chickens. We sell fresh eggs to local folks.We are avid gardeners, and have been selling our surplus veggies and fruit locally for a few years now. We strive to grow the best food available. We believe that with good management practices and quality natural inputs we can do just that. We do not raise any GMO foods. We also will not use petro-chemical fertilizers and pesticides. We use an integrated approach to pest management that includes monitoring for early signs of pests, the use of beneficial organisms and natural pest repellents and pesticides for control. Discovered through Walker County seat search (https://www.localharvest.org/huntsville-tx/farms). Listing last updated Jan 21, 2025. We are a local farm that produces super premium duck eggs, and more to come as we expand our homesteading efforts. We want to truly know our customers and know that we are feeding them and their children the highest quality product possible. Our birds are fed the highest quality feed available in our area, Texas Naturals (read more about their excellent feed at http://www.texasnaturalfeeds.com/). They are allowed to free range on a wonderful grass and clover mix, all day until they are penned up safely each evening. Frankly they are spoiled ducks that live a carefree happy life very few people could dream of and that is what it takes to product a product of this quality. Ducks eggs are much higher in nutritional value than chicken eggs (especially store bought eggs) and can often be eaten safely by those who have chicken egg allergies. You can learn more about how much more nutritious duck eggs are at http://www.localharvest.org/blog/16682/entry/duck_eggs_vs_chicken_eggs While store bought organic eggs are from chickens fed organic feed, from there it is still basically factory farming. The birds are confined indoors and never eat a real natural diet. Our ducks are on pasture daily

records.notes: Discovered through McCulloch County seat search (https://www.localharvest.org/brady-tx/farms). Listing last updated Jan 21, 2025. Wild Herd is our small, diversified family farm nestled in beautiful Texas Hill Country. We raise all heritage breeds of livestock, including pigs, turkeys, and cattle. They are rotated on native pasture their entire lives which allows them to live and thrive in healthful, wild conditions. Animal welfare and comfort is always our top priority. Beef cattle rotationally graze across 190 acres of diversified pastureland. Our pigs and turkeys eat a locally milled non-gmo, non-soy, non-corn grain ration. Thanksgiving turkeys are butchered on-farm in the fall to lessen transportation stress at time of slaughter. We never use any herbicides, pesticides, or synthetic fertilizers on our pastures. Meat animals are not given any hormones or antibiotics. Pork and beef is available by the share (whole or ½ for pork and whole, ½, ¼, ? for beef) or as individual cuts. Turkeys are available by pre-order in late summer for purchase of a whole bird for the holiday season. Check our website and Instagram (@wildherdtx) for availability updates. We can arrange drop-off points or home delivery throughout Central Texas, or you are also welcome to come check out the ranch and pick up on-farm.

We still proudly produce several wild honeys to choose from. Wild honey is made from nectar that comes from natural wild plants, vegetation and native growth. The production of wild honey is the way honeybees have provided food for man since biblical times and is an important dietary addition. We select pieces of land that are far from subdivisions & neighborhoods, then look for land that is not manicured, land that is kept in a more wild state. Expanding on a pre-existing but underused 5,000+ sq/ft garden, the produce side of Windy Hill began. Although we are not "certified" organic, we feel that the produce we grow goes well beyond the requirements of organic certification. In addition, we support the growth of local farms and markets and encourage others in their "organic" growing and selling. Discovered through Andrews County seat search (https://www.localharvest.org/andrews-tx/farms). Listing last updated Jan 21, 2025. The YT Ranch was founded in 1883 by my great-grandfather, A. W. Wight. Our family began practicing low input, sustainable agriculture shortly after A. W. drilled the first water well on the ranch he homesteaded at Goldsmith, TX before the beginning of the 20th. century. Through the five generations that our famiy has lived on the ranch, we have always adhered to the principle that the ranch has to be preserved in order to pass it on to the next generation. The hardships of ranching in the desert have taught us that if pastures are overgrazed, and neglected, it takes many years for the rangeland to recover. One of the tools that I use is Longhorn/Corriente cattle. They are an environmentally friendly breed, adapted to our harsh conditions. They require no supplemental feed, and their natural resistance to disease means that we do not have to treat any of them with antibiotics. Longhorn/corriente beef is lower in fat and cholesterol, yet is juicy and tender, and has abundant flavor.

Zanzenberg Farm is a family owned-operated, pasture-based, beyond organic, local-market farm and education outreach located in the Texas Hill Country near the Guadalupe River in Kerr County. We produce non-gmo, corn & soy free pastured pork and poultry while utilizing holistic management intensive pasture rotation, grazing and planning. We are proud to say we raise and breed Heritage pigs, including Gloucestershire Old Spots, Red Wattle and Hereford pigs. Heritage breeds are traditional livestock breeds - the ones raised in a bygone time by our forefathers before the industrial age. While heritage breeds once roamed America's pasturelands, they are now rare and in danger of extinction. Heritage breeds along with intense rotational grazing produce a healthier and much more flavorful, perfectly marbled pork which is unaffected by the hormone and antibiotic influence of industrialized breeding. Our product is sold at our on-farm store, our local farmers market and through direct email order/shipping in Texas only.
